# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns

Catalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks
(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to
prove the claimed mathematics. Complements
the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level
blockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the
trick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions
bake in*.

Every pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a
paper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all
cross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.

## Why this matters

Kernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:

- Be marked `\leanok` in the blueprint,
- Have a sorry-free proof body,
- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),

and still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof
obligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel
branch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this
codebase.

## Catalogue

- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)
- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)
- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)
- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)
- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)
- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)

---

## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis

**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own
conclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body
is a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no
mathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle
(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the
catalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by
PR [#491].

### Why it's bad

The theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;
the caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the
caller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the
stack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\leanok` tag
misrepresents the actual state of the proof.

### How to spot it

- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's
  conclusion.
- The proof body is one of:
  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`
  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`
  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`
- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,
  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.
- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).

### Concrete example

Historical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):

```lean
theorem mainInduction
    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)
    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :
    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,
      ConsRel strategy.state ...
        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by
  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩
  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩
  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩
```

Here `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type
`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally
the conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this
specific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed
the same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains
the archetypal example of the anti-pattern.

PR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's
fields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across
individual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse
because the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs
that discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped
existential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name
that suggests the paper result has been proved.

### How to fix it

Prefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses
— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's
conclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content
cannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation
to be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open
under a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as
an extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof
debt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not
the preferred shape for new work.

A signature passes the smell test if:

- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the
  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and
- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*
  theorem, not a trivially-false one.

### Related issues and patterns

- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker
- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue
- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by
  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly
- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)
- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern
- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation

---

## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand

**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and
a nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line
`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The "mathematical
content" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See
issues [#477], [#494].

### Why it's bad

`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen
*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` "proof" transports none of the
paper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to
match the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,
`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated
anywhere in Lean.

### How to spot it

- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where
  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.
- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a
  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a
  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.
- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting
  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.
- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function
  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field
  directly.

### Concrete example

From `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:

```lean
/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/
def fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)
    (α β : Point params) : Error :=
  if α = β then 1 else 0

/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/
lemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)
    (α β : Point params) :
    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl

/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/
theorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :
    (∀ α β : Point params,
      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro α β
    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta
  ...
```

The paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an
orthonormal basis under the actual inner product
`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum
identity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the
definition equals itself.

### Not every `rfl` is a castle

Distinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally
how something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in
`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of
`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is
elsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is
a naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper
identity, or does it just name a compound expression?**

### How to fix it

1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define
   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters
   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.
2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those
   concrete objects.
3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib
   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`
   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).
4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a
   consequence, not as the primitive.

### Related issues

- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)
- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates

---

## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions

**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else
default`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or
`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for "precondition not met." Downstream
theorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the
theorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the
obligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the
function. See issue [#495], related to [#307].

### Why it's bad

The signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a
non-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about "the output" is
proved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents working in `MIPStarRE`. This is the **single
source of truth** for agent conventions. Claude Code agents should also read
`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.

## Project Overview

This repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics
around $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of
[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is
the **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active
track is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\*=RE*
(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).

CI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and
merges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through
`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before
doing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the
rules.

Key locations:

- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\*=RE
  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in
  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and
  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`
- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\*
  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source
  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)
- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT
- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references
  (`\lean{}`, `\leanok`)
- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint
- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans
- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer

A legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.

**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):

1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint
3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold

Always read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The
paper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and
proof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a
sorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is
almost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first
understanding the paper's proof strategy.

## Repository Layout

```
MIPStarRE/
├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure
│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...
│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types
└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)
    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements
    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem
    ├── Preliminaries/
    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/
    ├── MainInductionStep/
    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/
    ├── GlobalVariance/
    ├── SelfImprovement/
    ├── CommutativityPoints/
    ├── Commutativity/
    └── Pasting/
```

Each LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports
flow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.

## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands

Run commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.

### First-time setup

```bash
lake exe cache get
lake build
scripts/install_git_hooks.sh
scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check
```

Run the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks
move fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync
checks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.

### Full project build (CI-equivalent)

```bash
lake build
```

### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)

```bash
lake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean
```

### Check for proof holes in one file

```bash
rg -n "sorry|axiom" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true
```

### Check for proof holes in the whole project

```bash
rg -n "sorry|axiom" MIPStarRE
```

### Declaration checker

```bash
lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls
```

Use this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.

### Blueprint build

```bash
leanblueprint pdf    # PDF output
leanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)
```

In CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.

### What counts as a single test

This repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest
single-test commands are:

- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and
  `rg -n "sorry|axiom" path/to/File.lean || true`
- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`
- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and
  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`

### Recommended validation sequence

For a Lean file change:

1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`
2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`
3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`

For blueprint changes:

1. Run `leanblueprint web`
2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`

## Toolchain

- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)
- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)

Important `lakefile.toml` options:

- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly
- `pp.unicode.fun = true`
- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`
- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`

## Proof-Filling Order

Sections must be filled in this dependency order:

1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries
2. Section 5: making measurements projective
3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance
4. Section 9: self-improvement
5. Sections 10–11: commutativity
6. Section 12: pasting
7. Section 6: main induction wrapper

Do not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.

## Faithful Formalization Policy

A declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean
statement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.
Changing a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in
`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a
faithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.
This applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper
result, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the
hypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose
conclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra
load-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not
the paper theorem.
The project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize
them as permanent infrastructure.

If the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must
not mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either
leave the source-labelled entry without `\leanok`, or state the restricted or
conditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are
displayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\leanok` only
against a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must
not be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.

When a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a
source theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.
The note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of
the cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,
deriving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.

This rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as
`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked
from the blueprint by `\lean{...}` and `\leanok`.

Before editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,
`prop:*`):

1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.
2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are
   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.
3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer
   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary
   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.
4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named
   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.
5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A
   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it
   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains
   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem
   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its
   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like
   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example
   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a
   name ending in `_ofObligations`.
6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper
   with `\leanok`.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:44:	The symmetrization argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:symmetric-strat} below invokes Naimark dilation in the form of Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark} (stated and proved in Chapter~\ref{chap:projective}): a bipartite state together with two sub-measurement families can be replaced, without changing any of the correlations $\bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}$, by a product-extended state together with projective sub-measurements on the enlarged spaces. 1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Distance
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistributionAux
     3	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.State
     4	
     5	/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness
     6	
     7	The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
     8	`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-237`,
     9	from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-288`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    17	
    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

results/telemetry/owner-audits/shadow-reviews/opus-review-pr137-e19f699.md:34:The mathematics in this packet is correct and the four relation families the issue asks for are all present, proved for arbitrary finite POVM strategies with the explicit constant `36 * ε` and in both directed orientations. What blocks merge is the shape of the API rather than its content. About three hundred of the seven hundred and fifty-eight new lines are game-generic probability infrastructure that has been welded to `msGame`, re-declares a private definition from the games layer, and is then re-exported through the stable public facade in direct contradiction of the issue's own scope note; three sibling soundness theorems take the same `1 - ε ≤ S.value` hypothesis and will each need a copy. Around that sit four smaller reuse and traceability defects: a second binary character alongside `phaseSign`, four duplicated forward/reverse helper proofs that the already-imported `msWinPredicate_symm` collapses, and the missing formalization-only marking that `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` §5.9 requires of exactly this kind of non-paper public lemma. Since this layer is the foundation the remaining children of #77 will be written against, the placement decision is worth making once, now.

results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr95-20260904-01.jsonl:15:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_6","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,280p' docs/anti_patterns.md\"","aggregated_output":"# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns\n\nCatalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks\n(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\nfaithful to the paper.\n\n### Circular reasoning\n\nLean's kernel forbids literal declaration cycles, so focus on **mathematical\ncircularity**:\n\n- Proofs that assume (or trivially reintroduce) the statement being proved as a\n  local hypothesis, then immediately close the goal from that hypothesis\n- Helper lemmas in the same file that essentially restate the main goal and are\n  only used to prove that goal\n- Local `have`/`let` bindings that are just the goal rephrased, used to solve\n  the goal without any real argument\n- Newly introduced `axiom` that makes a difficult statement trivially provable\n  without connecting to existing Mathlib / core theorems\n- Abuse of `unsafe` features to fabricate proofs instead of giving a genuine\n  derivation\n- `by exact h` where `h` came from an unjustified assumption identical to the\n  goal\n\n### Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)\n\nProofs that avoid grounding in Mathlib:\n\n- Custom re-declarations of standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., re-proving\n  `add_comm` instead of importing it)\n- `axiom` or `sorry`-based helper lemmas for facts that already exist in\n  Mathlib\n- Chains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core\n- `private` helper lemmas that duplicate Mathlib API (e.g., custom matrix\n  transpose lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n- Overly long proof chains replaceable by a single Mathlib lemma\n\nWhen flagging, perform an actual lookup (grep, `#find?`, `exact?`,\n`library_search`). Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\nfaithful to the paper.\n\n### Circular reasoning\n\nLean's kernel forbids literal declaration cycles, so focus on **mathematical\ncircularity**:\n\n- Proofs that assume (or trivially reintroduce) the statement being proved as a\n  local hypothesis, then immediately close the goal from that hypothesis\n- Helper lemmas in the same file that essentially restate the main goal and are\n  only used to prove that goal\n- Local `have`/`let` bindings that are just the goal rephrased, used to solve\n  the goal without any real argument\n- Newly introduced `axiom` that makes a difficult statement trivially provable\n  without connecting to existing Mathlib / core theorems\n- Abuse of `unsafe` features to fabricate proofs instead of giving a genuine\n  derivation\n- `by exact h` where `h` came from an unjustified assumption identical to the\n  goal\n\n### Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)\n\nProofs that avoid grounding in Mathlib:\n\n- Custom re-declarations of standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., re-proving\n  `add_comm` instead of importing it)\n- `axiom` or `sorry`-based helper lemmas for facts that already exist in\n  Mathlib\n- Chains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core\n- `private` helper lemmas that duplicate Mathlib API (e.g., custom matrix\n  transpose lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n- Overly long proof chains replaceable by a single Mathlib lemma\n\nWhen flagging, perform an actual lookup (grep, `#find?`, `exact?`,\n`library_search`). statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\n\nSigns to watch for:\n\n- Custom type definitions for objects connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\n- Definitions that \"work\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\n  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type with Mathlib, the\nscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\nprogress rather than enabling it.\n\n### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\n\nA theorem advertised as results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr82-20260904-02.jsonl:26:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_11","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,720p' docs/anti_patterns.md\"","aggregated_output":"# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns\n\nCatalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks\n(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\nthe preferred shape for new work.\n\nA signature passes the smell test if:\n\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\n\n### Related issues and patterns\n\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\n\n---\n\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\n\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. base)\n   100\t  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)\n   101\t      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)\n   102\t      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)\n   103\t      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)\n   104\t  deriving DecidableEq\n   105\t\n   106\t/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/\n   107\tdef DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind\n   108\t  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis\n   109\t  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal\n   110\t\n   111\t/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/\n   112\tdef DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m\n   113\t  | .axis _ index _ => index\n   114\t  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index\n   115\t\n   116\t/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/\n   117\tdef DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :\n   118\t    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D\n   119\t  | .axis base _ _ => base\n   120\t  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base\n   121\t\n   122\t/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/\n   123\tdef DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :\n   124\t    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=\n   125\t  match line with\n   126\t  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index\n   127\t  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction\n   128\t\n   129\t/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric\n   130\tdirection. -/\n   131\ttheorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :\n   132\t    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by\n   133\t  cases line with\n   134\t  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed\n   135\t  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed\n   136\t\n   137\t/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero\n   138\tinvariant. -/\n   139\ttheorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}\n   140\t    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :\n   141\t    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by\n   142\t  cases line with\n   143\t  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline\n   144\t  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero\n   145\t\n   146\t/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/\n   147\tnoncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}\n   148\t    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=\n   149\t  linePoints line.base line.direction\n   150\t\n   151\t/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/\n   152\tnoncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)\n   153\t    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=\n   154\t  let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index\n   155\t  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point\n   156\t  .axis base sample.index (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)\n   157\t\n   158\t/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical diagonal-line description. -/\n   159\tnoncomputable def directDLineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)\n   160\t    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=\n   161\t  let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction\n   162\t  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point\n   163\t  .diagonal base sample.index direction\n   164\t    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point) (by\n   165\t      intro j hj\n   166\t      change directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction j = 0\n   167\t      rw [directPrefixProjection, if_pos hj])\n   168\t\n   169\t/-- The axis-line/point law with a directly sampled coordinate index. -/\n   170\tnoncomputable def directALinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   171\t    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=\n   172\t  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>\n   173\t    (directALineDescOf D sample, sample.point)\n   174\t\n   175\t/-- The diagonal-line/point law with a directly sampled prefix index. -/\n   176\tnoncomputable def directDLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   177\t    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=\n   178\t  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>\n   179\t    (directDLineDescOf D sample, sample.point)\n   180\t\n   181\t/-- The equal mixture of the directly indexed axis and diagonal line-point\n   182\tlaws.  This is the replacement for the otherwise undefined extended-dimension\n   183\tinstance used at paper\n   184\t`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1020-1116`. -/\n   185\tnoncomputable def directLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   186\t    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=\n   187\t  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)\n   188\t    (directALinePointDist D) (directDLinePointDist D)\n   189\t\n   190\t/-- The directly indexed axis-line/point law is probabilistic. -/\n   191\ttheorem directALinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   192\t    (directALinePointDist D).IsProbability := by\n   193\t  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _\n   194\t\n   195\t/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line/point law is probabilistic. -/\n   196\ttheorem directDLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   197\t    (directDLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by\n   198\t  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _\n   199\t\n   200\t/-- The directly indexed line-point mixture is probabilistic. -/\n   201\ttheorem directLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   202\t    (directLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by\n   203\t  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _\n   204\t    (directALinePointDist_isProbability D) (directDLinePointDist_isProbability D)\n   205\t    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)\n   206\t\n   207\t/-- The point and stored-index marginals of the direct axis-line law are\n   208\tuniform.  This is a direct-index analogue of `lem:alnf`, required by\n   209\tthe repair described in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`;\n   210\tthe source distribution is at\n   211\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`.\n   212\t-/\n   213\ttheorem directALinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   214\t    (directALinePointDist D).map Prod.snd =\n   215\t        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧\n   216\t      (directALinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =\n   217\t        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by\n   218\t  sorry\n   219\t\n   220\t/-- Every sampled direct axis line contains its paired point.  This is the\n   221\tDirect-index incidence obligation corresponding to `lem:alnf` and\n   222\tthe repair in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/\n   223\ttheorem directALinePointDist_mem_line (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   224\t    ∀ sample ∈ (directALinePointDist D).support,\n   225\t      sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by\n   226\t  sorry\n   227\t\n   228\t/-- The point and stored-index marginals of the direct diagonal-line law are\n   229\tuniform.  This is the direct-index analogue of `lem:dlnf`, paper\n   230\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`,\n   231\tand is a named obligation in the dimension-divisibility repair. -/\n   232\ttheorem directDLinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   233\t    (directDLinePointDist D).map Prod.snd =\n   234\t        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧\n   235\t      (directDLinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =\n   236\t        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by\n   237\t  sorry\n   238\t\n   239\t/-- Every sampled direct diagonal line contains its paired point.  This is the\n   240\tDirect-index incidence obligation corresponding to `lem:dlnf`. -/\n   241\ttheorem directDLinePointDist_mem_line (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   242\t    ∀ sample ∈ (directDLinePointDist D).support,\n   243\t      sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by\n   244\t  sorry\n   245\t\n   246\t/-- A sampled direct diagonal direction vanishes below its stored prefix\n   247\tindex.  This is the direct counterpart of the third conclusion of\n   248\t`lem:dlnf`, paper\n   249\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`.\n   250\t-/\n   251\ttheorem directDLinePointDist_prefix_zero (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   252\t    ∀ sample ∈ (directDLinePointDist D).support,\n   253\t      ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < sample.1.index.val →\n   254\t        sample.1.direction j = 0 := by\n   255\t  sorry\n   256\t\n   257\tend\n   258\t\n   259\tend MIPStarRE.QPBT\n     1\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Geometry\n     2\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.LowDegreeGameTheorems\n     3\t\n     4\t/-!\n     5\t# The directly indexed low-degree game\n     6\t\n     7\tThis module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game\n     8\tfor the directly indexed low-degree interface.\n     9\t\n    10\t## References\n    11\t\n    12\tThe underlying game is `def:ld-game` in\n    13\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin\n    14\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.\n    15\t-/\n    16\t\n    17\topen scoped BigOperators\n    18\t\n    19\tnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n    20\t\n    21\topen MIPStarRE.LDT\n    22\topen MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries\n    23\topen MIPStarRE.Quantum\n    24\t\n    25\tnoncomputable section\n    26\t\n    27\t/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the\n    28\tdirect scalar field. -/\n    29\tabbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=\n    30\t  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D\n    31\t\n    32\t/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line\n    33\tand every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause\n    34\tkeeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/\n    35\tdef DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)\n    36\t    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)\n    37\t    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=\n    38\t  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧\n    39\t    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →\n    40\t      evalCoefficient f t = a\n    41\t\n    42\t/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an\n    43\texplicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field\n    44\tvalue is used as a fallback. -/\n    45\tnoncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}\n    46\t    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)\n    47\t    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by\n    48\t  classical\n    49\t  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then\n    50\t    some (Classical.choose h)\n    51\t  else none\n    52\t\n    53\t/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/\n    54\tabbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D\n    55\t\n    56\t/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant\n    57\tcoordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and\n    58\taxis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/\n    59\tnoncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :\n    60\t    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D\n    61\t  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩\n    62\t  | .aline, sample =>\n    63\t      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index\n    64\t      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩\n    65\t  | .dline, sample =>\n    66\t      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction\n    67\t      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩\n    68\t\n    69\t/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform\n    70\tordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample\n    71\tcontains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/\n    72\tnoncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :\n    73\t    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=\n    74\t  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>\n    75\t    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),\n    76\t      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))\n    77\t\n    78\t/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/\n    79\ttheorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :\n    80\t    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by\n    81\t  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability\n    82\t    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _\n    83\t\n    84\t/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/\n    85\tinductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where\n    86\t  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)\n    87\t  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)\n    88\t  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)\n    89\t  deriving DecidableEq\n    90\t\n    91\t/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/\n    92\tabbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=\n    93\t  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕\n    94\t    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕\n    95\t      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))\n    96\t\n    97\t/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and\n    98\tits finite code. -/\n    99\tnoncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   100\t    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where\n   101\t  toFun\n   102\t    | .pointVals a => .inl a\n   103\t    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)\n   104\t    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)\n   105\t  invFun\n   106\t    | .inl a => .pointVals a\n   107\t    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a\n   108\t    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a\n   109\t  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl\n   110\t  right_inv := by\n   111\t    intro answer\n   112\t    rcases answer with a | a\n   113\t    · rfl\n   114\t    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl\n   115\t\n   116\tinstance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=\n   117\t  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩\n   118\t\n   119\tnoncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=\n   120\t  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm\n   121\t\n   122\t/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its\n   123\tquestion type. -/\n   124\tdef validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)\n   125\t    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=\n   126\t  match t, answer with\n   127\t  | .point, .pointVals _ => true\n   128\t  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true\n   129\t  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true\n   130\t  | _, _ => false\n   131\t\n   132\t/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/\n   133\tdef directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)\n   134\t    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)\n   135\t    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)\n   136\t    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=\n   137\t  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,\n   138\t    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →\n   139\t      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j\n   140\t\n   141\t/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/\n   142\tdef directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)\n   143\t    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)\n   144\t    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)\n   145\t    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=\n   146\t  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,\n   147\t    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →\n   148\t      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j\n   149\t\n   150\t/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from\n   151\t`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line\n   152\tquestion. -/\n   153\tnoncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   154\t    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →\n   155\t      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=\n   156\t  open Classical in\n   157\t  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>\n   158\t    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then\n   159\t      match tA, tB, a, b with\n   160\t      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)\n   161\t      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>\n   162\t          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)\n   163\t      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>\n   164\t          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)\n   165\t      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>\n   166\t          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)\n   167\t      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>\n   168\t          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)\n   169\t      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)\n   170\t      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)\n   171\t      | _, _, _, _ => true\n   172\t    else false\n   173\t\n   174\t/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.\n   175\tIt is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game\n   176\t`ldGame`. -/\n   177\tnoncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where\n   178\t  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D\n   179\t  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D\n   180\t  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D\n   181\t  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D\n   182\t  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D\n   183\t  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D\n   184\t  decide := directLdWinPredicate D\n   185\t\n   186\t/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/\n   187\tdef directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)\n   188\t    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=\n   189\t  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)\n   190\t\n   191\t/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.\n   192\tWrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for\n   193\t`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/\n   194\tdef directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :\n   195\t    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D\n   196\t  | .pointVals values => values\n   197\t  | .alinePolys _ => 0\n   198\t  | .dlinePolys _ => 0\n   199\t\n   200\t/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed\n   201\tgame. -/\n   202\tnoncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=\n   203\t  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d\n   204\t\n   205\t/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/\n   206\tnoncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)\n   207\t    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=\n   208\t  Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι\n   209\t\n   210\t/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/\n   211\tdef evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}\n   212\t    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :\n   213\t    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=\n   214\t  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1\n   215\t\n   216\tend\n   217\t\n   218\tend MIPStarRE.QPBT\n     1\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Game\n     2\t\n     3\t/-!\n     4\t# Soundness for the directly indexed low-degree game\n     5\t\n     6\tThis module isolates the quantum soundness obligation for the directly indexed\n     7\tlow-degree 19\topen MIPStarRE.LDT\n    20\topen MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries\n    21\topen MIPStarRE.Quantum\n    22\t\n    23\tnoncomputable section\n    24\t\n    25\t/-- Quantum soundness obligation for the directly indexed low-degree game.\n    26\tThis is the repaired import form proposed in\n    27\t`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, needed by the Chapter 15\n    28\tcombining argument at paper\n    29\t`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1288`.\n    30\t\n    31\tThis is a formalization auxiliary assertion, not the source-labelled\n [Paper-gap documentation pattern](#pattern-6-paper-gap-documentation-pattern)\n\n---\n\n## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations\n\n### The rule\n\nA declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,\nproposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal\nencoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are\nboth part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,\nobligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present\nin the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.\n\nThe project therefore distinguishes three objects.\n\n| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |\n|--------|------------------|------------------|\n| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\\lean{}`; statement-level `\\leanok` only when the statement matches |\n| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |\n| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\\leanok` |\n\nIt is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented\nas the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly\npoint, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,\nor remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the\nconditional helper is given a different name.\n\nThe preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or\ndefinition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked\n`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement\nof a source-labelled theorem.\n\n### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily\n\n| Temporary reason | Explanation |\n|------------------|-------------|\n| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |\n| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |\n| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |\n\nThese reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain\nwhy a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses\nare being actively removed.\n\n### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input\n\n1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in\n   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.\n2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses\n   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or\n   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to\n   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,\n   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic\n   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited\n   statement says so.\n3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical\n   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation. The declaration\nshould carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper\ndependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the\ninternal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation\nwith a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the\nmissing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem\nstatement.\n\n### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations\n\nA new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,\n`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,\n`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in\nthe def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the\nreviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper\nstatement or a Lean-only proof obligation.\n\nUse one of the following markers.\n\n| Marker | Use |\n|--------|-----|\n| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |\n| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |\n| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |\n| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |\n| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |\n\nProof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note\nor tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.\nIf such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis\nto a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement\nand leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.\n\n### Conditional helper boundary\n\n1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a\n   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first\n   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof\n   open. The correct\n   boundary is now the theorem `selfImprovement`, whose missing\n   proof is an explicit `sorry`.\n\n   The former induction-section helper\n   `selfImprovementInInductionSection_ofObligations` was removed because it\n   encouraged propagation of the Section 9 bundle into the Section 6 successor\n   constructors.  Those constructors now call the theorem\n   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` directly; its current proof gap is the\n   correct place for the missing work.\n\n3. **Propagation is a warning sign.**  The consumer of\n   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` — typically a\n   `MainInductionStep` theorem — should close the hypothesis with an internal\n   theorem as soon as possible. Bridge, residual, repair, and proof-obligation inputs must be\n   produced inside its proof rather than added to its statement.\n\n### Existing bridge-like declarations\n\nSeveral older declarations still name proof obligations explicitly.  They are\ntransitional proof debt, not a pattern to extend to paper theorem statements.\nWhen such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and\nkept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.\n\n| Declaration | Status to maintain |\n|-------------|--------------------|\n| `LdPastingNontrivialContext` | Nontrivial-regime context for `ldPastingNontrivial`; do not present it as the unrestricted `thm:ld-pasting` context |\n| `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` | Restricted nontrivial-regime form of `thm:ld-pasting`; link from a Lean-only remark, while `Pasting.ldPasting` remains the unrestricted source-facing theorem |\n\nThe former same-carrier `mainFormal` transport-witness route has been retired.\nThe former `SelfImprovement.HelperStrongSelfConsistencyInput`,\n`SelfImprovement.OrthonormalizationInput`, `SelfImprovement.FinalFieldsInput`, and\n`MakingMeasurementsProjective.OrthonormalizationInput` bundles have been removed.\nUseful proof content should be kept as named construction lemmas, while missing\northonormalization or final-field arguments remain direct proof gaps on the\nsource-facing theorem until proved from the paper hypotheses.\n\nThe former `MakingMeasurementsProjective.SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation\nhas likewise been retired. It is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited\n   outside result.\n2. No current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated.\n3. Prefer the cheapest mechanism that\n   holds the invariant.\n5. **Two memory disciplines.** Reports and session records are append-only and\n   never rewritten (supersede with dated status notes). Protocol documents\n   and paper-gap notes are living documents that are rewritten in place\n   (history lives in git and `EVOLUTION.md`). Do not mix the two.\n\n## Amendment procedure\n\n1. Write the incident/observation in `results/telemetry/events.md` (dated).\n2. Draft the protocol edit.\n3. Append to `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`:\n   `## YYYY-MM-DD — <short title>` with fields **Trigger** (cite events.md\n   entry or telemetry line), **Change** (files + gist), **Expected effect**,\n   and, when known later, **Outcome**.\n4. Commit protocol edit and ledger entry together, `docs(local)` scope.\n5. If the change alters guard semantics (locks, caps, gates, kill switches),\n   grep `local/` for every enforcement point and update all of them in the\n   same commit — the parent repo maintained such consistency invariants\n   through cross-referencing comments; we inherit the same drift risk.\n\n## Telemetry duties\n\nSchemas (all JSONL, one object per line; timestamps ISO-8601 with offset):\n\n- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` —\n  `{ts, stage, event: start|end|milestone, note?, tokens_note?}`\n  Stages: `1-skeleton`, `2-references`, `3-blueprint`, `4.1-minimal`,\n  `4.2-full-skeleton`, `4.3-proofs` (extend as needed).\n- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` —\n  `{name, role, issue, pr?, thread_id, start, end, wall_s,\n    usage: {input, cached_input, cache_write, output, reasoning},\n    exit, dispatcher, worktree, status: active|done|failed|archived}`\n  Written only by `local/bin/dispatch.sh` / `telemetry.py`.\n- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` —\n  `{ts, kind: warm|rebuild|cache-get|ci-build, trigger, seconds, outcome,\n    sha?, note?}`\n- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated bullets; free prose; one incident per\n  bullet: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.\n\nDuties:\n\n- **Every agent session goes through `dispatch.sh`** so token usage and wall\n  time land in `sessions.jsonl`.
