     1	
     2	\section{Making measurements projective}
     3	\label{sec:making-measurements-projective}
     4	
     5	A recurring theme in $\MIP^*$ research is that 
     6	projective measurements are significantly easier to manipulate
     7	than general POVM measurements.
     8	As just one example among many,
     9	when $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ are projective measurements,
    10	the ``$\approx_\delta$" and ``$\simeq_\delta$" distances are equivalent.
    11	In other words:
    12	\begin{equation*}
    13	A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a
    14	\qquad
    15	\iff
    16	\qquad
    17	A^x_a \ot I \approx_{2\delta} I \ot B^x_a.
    18	\end{equation*}
    19	This is Fact~$4.13$ from~\cite{NW19}.
    20	On the other hand when~$A$ and~$B$
    21	are not projective,
    22	one can find examples of measurements
    23	where $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$
    24	for $\delta \rightarrow 0$
    25	but one can show $A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^x_a$
    26	only for $\eps \rightarrow 1$;
    27	this is Remark~$4.15$ from~\cite{NW19}.
    28	As a result, it is important to be able to convert
    29	POVM measurements to projective measurements
    30	whenever possible.
    31	
    32	In this section, we will survey two tools for doing so.
    33	The first of these is the textbook Naimark dilation theorem.
    34	In our setting, it states the following.
    35	
    36	\begin{theorem}[Naimark dilation]\label{thm:naimark}
    37	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    38	Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}}$
    39	and $B=\{B^y_b\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    40	Then there exists
    41	\begin{enumerate}
    42	\item Hilbert spaces $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$ and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    43	\item a state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    44	\item and two measurements  $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}^x_a\}$ and $\widehat{B}=\{\widehat{B}^y_b\}$
    45	acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    46	and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    47	respectively,
    48	\end{enumerate}
    49	such that the following is true.
    50	If we write $\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}$,
    51	then for all $x,y, a, b$,
    52	 \begin{equation*}
    53	 \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}
    54	 = \bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat{A}^x_a \ot \widehat{B}^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}.
    55	 \end{equation*}
    56	 In addition, $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$ is a \emph{product state},
    57	 meaning that we can write it as
    58	 \begin{equation*}
    59	 \ket{\mathsf{aux}}= \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}},
    60	 \end{equation*}
    61	for $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    62	and $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$.
    63	\end{theorem}
    64	The second of these is the ``orthogonalization lemma" from~\cite{KV11}.
    65	In the setting of symmetric strategies, it states the following.
    66	
    67	\begin{theorem}[Orthogonalization lemma]\label{thm:orthonormalization}
    68	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state,
    69	and let $A = \{A_a\}$ be a sub-measurement with strong self-consistency
    70	\begin{equation*}
    71	\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_a \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\zeta.
    72	\end{equation*}
    73	Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $P = \{P_a\}$ such that
    74	\begin{equation*}
    75	A_a \otimes I \approx_{100 \zeta^{1/4}} P_a \otimes I.
    76	\end{equation*}
    77	\end{theorem}
    78	
    79	These two results serve largely the same purpose,
    80	and for our applications it will typically suffice to use either one.
    81	That said, there are tradeoffs when choosing to use one or the other.
    82	Naimark dilation is convenient because it can be applied to any family of sub-measurements
    83	and it preserves measurement outcome probabilities exactly.
    84	On the other hand, it requires swapping out the state $\ket{\psi}$ and measurements~$A$ and~$B$
    85	for $\ket{\widehat{\psi}}$ and $\widehat{A}$ and $\widehat{B}$, respectively,
    86	which can be notationally cumbersome.
    87	Most works opt to skip adding the hats,
    88	and instead say something to the effect of ``using Naimark, we can assume that~$A$ and~$B$ are projective."
    89	However, there is subtlety in doing so,
    90	which is that Naimark dilation does not necessarily preserve ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements;
    91	in other words, $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$
    92	does not necessarily imply $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$.
    93	(As an example, \Cref{ex:easy-but-long} below
    94	provides a case in which $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{0} I \ot B^x_a$,
    95	but $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$ only holds for $\delta \geq 1$.)
    96	This can lead to trouble if the same notation is used for~$A, B$ and $\widehat{A}, \widehat{B}$,
    97	as ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements derived before applying Naimark might not necessarily hold after applying Naimark.
    98	(That said, as pointed out at the end of Section~$4.4$ of~\cite{NW19},
    99	``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements are often derived as a consequence of ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements.
   100	And as Naimark preserves ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements,
   101	one could use them to simply rederive any ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements post-Naimark.)
   102	
   103	The downsides of using the orthogonalization lemma
   104	are that it can only be applied to measurements which are strongly self-consistent
   105	and it introduces additional error.
   106	As we will see below, its proof is significantly more complicated than Naimark dilation.
   107	On the plus side, it has none of the notational baggage that Naimark brings,
   108	and so it is more concrete to use.
   109	In addition, it can lead to stronger results,
   110	as it does not require introducing an auxiliary state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$.
   111	
   112	In this work, we will opt to use the orthogonalization lemma rather than Naimark dilation.
   113	However, we will include proofs of both for completeness.
   114	We will prove \Cref{thm:naimark} in \Cref{sec:naimark}
   115	and then \Cref{thm:orthonormalization} in \Cref{sec:orthogonalization}.
   116	
   117	\subsection{Naimark dilation}\label{sec:naimark}
   118	
   119	To prove \Cref{thm:naimark}, we will first need the following lemma.
   120	
   121	\begin{lemma}
   122	  \label{lem:naimark-helper}
   123	  Let $A = \{A_{a}\}$ be a sub-measurement with $k$ distinct outcomes $a \in \calA$, and let $\ket{\mathsf{aux}} \in \C^{k+1}$ be any state. Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}_{a}\}$ such that
   124	  for each outcome~$a$,
   125	  \[ (I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot \widehat{A}_{a} \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) =
   126	    A_{a}. \]
   127	\end{lemma}
   128	\begin{proof}
   129	We will consider an orthonormal basis for $\C^{k+1}$
   130	consisting of a vector $\ket{a}$ for each $a \in \calA$ and the vector $\ket{\bot}$.
   131	Let~$U$ be any unitary such that for each vector $\ket{\psi} \in \C^d$,
   132	\begin{align*}
   133	U \cdot (\ket{\psi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   134	&= \sum_{a \in \calA} ((A_{a})^{1/2} \ket{\psi}) \ot \ket{a} + ((1 - A)^{1/2}\ket{\psi}) \ot \ket{\bot}\\
   135	&= \Big(\sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}\Big)
   136			\cdot \ket{\psi}.
   137	\end{align*}
   138	This implies that
   139	\begin{equation*}
   140	U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   141	= \sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}.
   142	\end{equation*}
   143	Hence, for any $a \in \calA$,
   144	\begin{equation*}
   145	(I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   146	= (I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot \Big(\sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}\Big)
   147	= (A_a)^{1/2}.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	  Then the desired projective sub-measurement is
   150	  \[ \widehat{A}_a = U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U. \]
   151	  This is because
   152	\begin{align*}
   153	 (I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot \widehat{A}_{a} \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   154	&=(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot (U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U) \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\
   155	&=(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a}) \cdot (I\ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\
   156	&= (A_a)^{1/2} \cdot (A_a)^{1/2} = A_a.
   157	\end{align*}
   158	This completes the proof.
   159	\end{proof}
   160	
   161	Now we prove \Cref{thm:naimark}.
   162	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:naimark}]
   163	For each $x$, let $k$ be the number of outcomes in $A^x$,
   164	and let $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}}$ be a state of dimensionality $k+1$.
   165	Let $\widetilde{A}^x$ be the sub-measurement guaranteed by \Cref{lem:naimark-helper}.
   166	Define $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},x}}$ and $\widetilde{B}^x$ similarly.
   167	We define
   168	\begin{equation*}
   169	\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \ot \big(\ot_{x} \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}}\big)
   170						\ot \big(\ot_{x} \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},x}}\big)
   171	\end{equation*}
   172	and
   173	\begin{align*}
   174	\widehat{A}^x_a
   175	&= \widetilde{A}^x_a \ot \big(\ot_{z \neq x} I_{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},z}}\big)\\
   176	\widehat{B}^y_b
   177	&= \widetilde{B}^y_b \ot \big(\ot_{z\neq y} I_{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},z}}\big).
   178	\end{align*}
   179	Then for all $x,y,z,b$,
   180	\begin{align*}
   181	\bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat{A}^x_a \ot \widehat{B}^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}
   182	& = \bra{\psi} \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}} \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},y}}
   183		\cdot \widetilde{A}^x_a \ot \widetilde{B}^y_b \cdot \ket{\psi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},y}}\\
   184	&= 	\bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}.
   185	\end{align*}
   186	This completes the proof.
   187	\end{proof}
   188	
   189	\begin{example}[Naimark does not preserve ``$\approx_{\delta}$'']\label{ex:easy-but-long}
   190	We now carry out a simple example
   191	in which Naimark preserves ``$\simeq_\delta$'' statements without preserving ``$\approx_\delta$'' statements.
   192	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be an arbitrary state in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$,
   193	where $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} = \calH_{\mathrm{B}} = \C^d$.
   194	In addition, let $A = \{A_0, A_1\}$ and $B = \{B_0, B_1\}$ be the two-outcome measurements
   195	in which $A_0 = A_1 = B_0 = B_1 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot I_{d \times d}$.
   196	Then
   197	\begin{align*}
   198	\sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A_a \ot B_b\ket{\psi}
   199	&= \bra{\psi} A_0 \ot B_1\ket{\psi} + \bra{\psi} A_1 \ot B_0\ket{\psi}\\
   200	&= \frac{1}{4} \cdot \bra{\psi} I \ot I \ket{\psi} + \frac{1}{4} \cdot \bra{\psi} I \ot I \ket{\psi}
   201	= \frac{1}{2},
   202	\end{align*}
   203	and so $A_a \ot I \simeq_{1/2} I \ot A_a$.
   204	In addition,
   205	\begin{equation*}
   206	\sum_a \Vert (A_a \ot I - I \ot B_a) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2
   207	= \sum_a \Big\Vert \Big(\frac{1}{2} \cdot I \ot I - \frac{1}{2} \cdot I \ot I\Big) \ket{\psi}\Big\Vert^2
   208	= 0,
   209	\end{equation*}
   210	and so $A_a \ot I \approx_0 I \ot B_a$.
   211	
   212	Now we carry out the steps of Naimark dilation.
   213	Because~$A$ and~$B$ are two-outcome,
   214	we will set $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}} = \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}} = \C^2$,
   215	spanned by the basis vectors $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{1}$.
   216	(\Cref{lem:naimark-helper} actually asks that the auxiliary space have dimension $2+1 = 3$,
   217	where the third dimension is spanned by the basis vector $\ket{\bot}$.
   218	However, this is unnecessary for this example because~$A$ and~$B$
   219	are measurements rather than sub-measurements.)
   220	We will choose our two local auxiliary states
   221	to be
   222	\begin{equation*}
   223	\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} = \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}}
   224		= \ket{+} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{0} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{1}.
   225	\end{equation*}
   226	We first construct $\widehat{A}$ by following the proof of \Cref{lem:naimark-helper}.
   227	To begin, it asks for~$U$ to be a unitary such that for any $\ket{\phi}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}}$,
   228	\begin{align*}

    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}

   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,

   115	  players' registers.

   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.

   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:

   123	  \]

    44	\section{Key theorem forms}
    45	
    46	Three statements must be kept apart.  Throughout, $\game$ denotes a symmetric
    47	two-player one-round game and $\eps \ge 0$ a real parameter; the notation is

    50	\begin{enumerate}
    51	  \item \textbf{Source form (attainment form).}  If
    52	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and projective
    53	  strategy $\strategy$ with $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps$.
    54	  \item \textbf{Approximate form (what the source proof establishes).}  If
    55	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then for every $\eps' > \eps$ there exists a
    56	  symmetric and projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    57	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps'$.
    58	  \item \textbf{Given-strategy form (value-preserving symmetrization).}  If
    59	  $\strategy'$ is any strategy for $\game$ with
    60	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and
    61	  projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    62	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$.

    80	$\strategy = (\ket\psi, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector $\ket\psi$ in a
    81	tensor product $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ of \emph{finite-dimensional}
    82	Hilbert spaces together with POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ for the two
    83	players; its value $\val^*(\game, \strategy)$ is the acceptance probability,
    84	and the value of the game is the supremum
    85	\begin{equation*}
    86	  \val^*(\game) = \sup_{\strategy} \val^*(\game, \strategy)
    87	\end{equation*}
    88	over all tensor product strategies.  A strategy is projective if all its
    89	measurements are projective, and symmetric if the state is
    90	permutation-invariant on $\mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ and both players use the
    91	same measurements.
    92	
    93	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
    94	\footnote{The statement is at
    95	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
    96	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement restored to this form
    97	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
    98	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
    99	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   100	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   101	\begin{equation*}
   102	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   103	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   104	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   105	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   106	\end{equation*}
   107	
   108	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   109	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   110	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   111	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   112	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   113	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   114	\begin{equation*}
   115	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   116	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   117	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   118	\end{equation*}
   119	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   120	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   121	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   122	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   123	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   124	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   125	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   126	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   127	
   128	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   129	
   130	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   131	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   132	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   133	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   134	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   135	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   136	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   137	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   138	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   139	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   140	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   141	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   142	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   143	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   144	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   145	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   146	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   147	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   148	form.
   149	
   150	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   151	
   152	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   153	
   154	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   155	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   156	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   157	generality that it is projective.%
   158	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   159	lines~317--321.}
   160	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   161	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   162	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   163	
   164	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   165	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   166	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   167	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   168	lines~2322--2332.}
   169	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   170	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   171	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   172	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   173	not used.
   174	
   175	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   176	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   177	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   178	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint currently records the lemma as part of
   179	the games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on it; the two source
   180	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   181	development.  Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here
   182	--- requires the attainment form.
   183	
   184	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   185	
   186	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states the lemma in the source shape.
   187	Its proof records the value-preserving construction and the approximate form
   188	that the construction yields, and explicitly marks the remaining attainment
   189	step as unproved, citing this note; an accompanying remark summarizes the
   190	obstruction.  An earlier revision of the blueprint had instead weakened the
   191	source-labelled conclusion to the approximate form; following the project's
   192	proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled statement is restored and the missing
   193	step is tracked in the proof rather than absorbed into the statement. The
   194	source-shaped declaration \leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy} is
   195	now linked to the lemma; its proof remains the tracked attainment obligation.
   196	
   197	\section{Conclusion}
   198	
   199	The verdict is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma: the symmetrization
   200	argument proves the given-strategy and approximate forms, while the printed
   201	conclusion additionally asserts that the supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ is
   202	attained, which does not follow.  The gap is harmless for the results built on
   203	the lemma, since both uses in the source, and all planned uses in this
   204	project, proceed from a given strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ or from a
   205	strict lower bound on the value, for which the value-preserving construction
   206	suffices.  For stage~4 (formalization) the recommendation is: formalize the
   207	given-strategy symmetrization lemma as the workhorse statement; keep the
   208	source-labelled lemma in source shape with the attainment step an explicit,
   209	tracked proof obligation; and do not strengthen the source-labelled statement's
   210	hypotheses or weaken its conclusion silently.  If a later investigation
   211	settles the counterexample question for symmetric games, the statement should
   212	then be reclassified from an unproved step to a documented statement
   213	correction.

    93	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
    94	\footnote{The statement is at
    95	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
    96	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement restored to this form
    97	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
    98	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
    99	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   100	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   101	\begin{equation*}
   102	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   103	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   104	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   105	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   106	\end{equation*}
   107	
   108	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   109	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   110	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   111	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   112	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   113	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   114	\begin{equation*}
   115	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   116	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   117	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   118	\end{equation*}
   119	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   120	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   121	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   122	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   123	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   124	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   125	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   126	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   127	
   128	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   129	
   130	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   131	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   132	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   133	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   134	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   135	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   136	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   137	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   138	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   139	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   140	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   141	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   142	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   143	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   144	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   145	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   146	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   147	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   148	form.
   149	
   150	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   151	
   152	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   153	
   154	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   155	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   156	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   157	generality that it is projective.%
   158	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   159	lines~317--321.}
   160	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   161	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   162	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   163	
   164	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   165	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   166	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   167	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   168	lines~2322--2332.}
   169	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   170	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   171	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   172	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   173	not used.
   174	
   175	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   176	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   177	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   178	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint currently records the lemma as part of
   179	the games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on it; the two source
   180	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   181	development.  Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here
   182	--- requires the attainment form.
   183	
   184	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   185	
   186	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states the lemma in the source shape.
   187	Its proof records the value-preserving construction and the approximate form
   188	that the construction yields, and explicitly marks the remaining attainment
   189	step as unproved, citing this note; an accompanying remark summarizes the
   190	obstruction.  An earlier revision of the blueprint had instead weakened the
   191	source-labelled conclusion to the approximate form; following the project's
   192	proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled statement is restored and the missing
   193	step is tracked in the proof rather than absorbed into the statement. The
   194	source-shaped declaration \leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy} is
   195	now linked to the lemma; its proof remains the tracked attainment obligation.
   196	
   197	\section{Conclusion}
   198	
   199	The verdict is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma: the symmetrization
   200	argument proves the given-strategy and approximate forms, while the printed
   201	conclusion additionally asserts that the supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ is
   202	attained, which does not follow.  The gap is harmless for the results built on
   203	the lemma, since both uses in the source, and all planned uses in this
   204	project, proceed from a given strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ or from a
   205	strict lower bound on the value, for which the value-preserving construction
   206	suffices.  For stage~4 (formalization) the recommendation is: formalize the
   207	given-strategy symmetrization lemma as the workhorse statement; keep the
   208	source-labelled lemma in source shape with the attainment step an explicit,
   209	tracked proof obligation; and do not strengthen the source-labelled statement's
   210	hypotheses or weaken its conclusion silently.  If a later investigation
   211	settles the counterexample question for symmetric games, the statement should
   212	then be reclassified from an unproved step to a documented statement
   213	correction.

+/-- The real quadratic form of an operator evaluated on a finite vector. -/
+private def vectorQForm {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) (A : Op I) : ℝ :=
+  (inner ℂ ψ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A ψ)).re
+
+/-- Embed a bipartite state into the distinguished Naimark ancilla coordinates. -/
+private def padState
+    {I J α β : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((I × Option α) × (J × Option β)) :=
+  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((I × Option α) × (J × Option β)) ℂ).symm
+    (fun p => if p.1.2 = none ∧ p.2.2 = none then ψ.ofLp (p.1.1, p.2.1) else 0)
+
+/-- Padding a state by zero ancilla coordinates preserves its norm. -/
+private theorem padState_norm
+    {I J α β : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
+    ‖padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖ := by
+  apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp
+  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
+  simp [padState, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+
+/-- The padded-state quadratic form depends only on the distinguished
+compression of each local operator. -/
+private theorem stateQForm_padState
+    {I J α β : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
+    (A : Op I) (B : Op J)
+    (A' : Op (I × Option α)) (B' : Op (J × Option β))
+    (hA : ∀ i j, A' (i, none) (j, none) = A i j)
+    (hB : ∀ i j, B' (i, none) (j, none) = B i j) :
+    vectorQForm (padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ) (heteroKron A' B') =
+      vectorQForm ψ (heteroKron A B) := by
+  unfold vectorQForm
+  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
+  change Complex.re (∑ p : (I × Option α) × (J × Option β),
+      (∑ q : (I × Option α) × (J × Option β),
+        heteroKron A' B' p q *
+          (padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ).ofLp q) *
+        star (padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ).ofLp p) =
+    Complex.re (∑ p : I × J,
+      (∑ q : I × J, heteroKron A B p q * ψ.ofLp q) * star ψ.ofLp p)
+  simp [padState, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Fintype.sum_prod_type, hA, hB]
+
+/-- Choose the one-measurement Naimark dilation data for a POVM. -/
+private def oneMeasData
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) : OneMeasNaimarkData α I :=
+  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
+
+/-- The source submeasurement of the chosen Naimark data is the original POVM. -/
+private theorem oneMeasData_source_effect
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) :
+    (oneMeasData M).source.effect = M.effect := by
+  exact congrArg MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement.effect
+    (Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement))
+
+/-- Complete the Naimark projectors at one outcome to obtain a projective POVM. -/
+private def dilatedMeasurement
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (a₀ : α) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (I × Option α) :=
+  let P := completeAtOutcomeProj (oneMeasData M).toProjSubMeas a₀
+  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne P.outcome P.outcome_pos <| by
+    rw [P.sum_eq_total, P.total_eq_one]
+
+/-- Every effect of the completed Naimark measurement is a projection. -/
+private theorem dilatedMeasurement_isProjective
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (a₀ : α) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) :
+    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (dilatedMeasurement a₀ M) := by
+  intro a
+  let P := completeAtOutcomeProj (oneMeasData M).toProjSubMeas a₀
+  change IsProj (P.outcome a)
+  exact
+    { isIdempotentElem := P.proj a
+      isSelfAdjoint :=
+        (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (P.outcome_pos a)).isHermitian.eq }
+
+/-- Compressing a completed Naimark effect to the distinguished ancilla
+coordinate recovers the original POVM effect. -/
+private theorem dilatedMeasurement_compression
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (a₀ a : α) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) (i j : I) :
+    (dilatedMeasurement a₀ M).effect a (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect a i j := by
+  let D := oneMeasData M
+  let P := D.toProjSubMeas
+  have hcompress (b : α) : P.outcome b (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect b i j := by
+    change D.liftedEffect (some b) (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect b i j
+    rw [D.compression_none_none]
+    exact congrArg (fun X : Op I => X i j)
+      (congrFun (oneMeasData_source_effect M) b)
+  have htotal : P.total (i, none) (j, none) = (1 : Op I) i j := by
+    rw [← P.sum_eq_total]
+    simp_rw [Matrix.sum_apply, hcompress]
+    simpa [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrArg (fun X : Op I => X i j) M.sum_eq_one
+  simp only [dilatedMeasurement, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne]
+  change ((completeAtOutcomeProj P a₀).toMeasurement).outcome a
+      (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect a i j
+  rw [completeAtOutcomeProj_toMeasurement]
+  simp only [completeAtOutcome]
+  by_cases ha : a = a₀
+  · subst a
+    rw [dif_pos rfl]
+    rw [Matrix.add_apply, hcompress, Matrix.sub_apply, Matrix.one_apply, htotal]
+    by_cases hij : i = j <;> simp [hij, Matrix.one_apply]
+  · rw [dif_neg ha]
+    exact hcompress a

+/-- A unit vector has a nonempty coordinate type. -/
+private theorem nonempty_of_unit_vector
+    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) : Nonempty I := by
+  classical
+  by_contra hI
+  haveI : IsEmpty I := not_nonempty_iff.mp hI
+  have hzero : ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
+  rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hψ
+  norm_num at hψ
+
+/-- A POVM on a nonzero finite-dimensional space has an outcome. -/
+private theorem measurement_outcome_nonempty
+    {α I : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Nonempty I]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) : Nonempty α := by
+  classical
+  by_contra hα
+  haveI : IsEmpty α := not_nonempty_iff.mp hα
+  let i : I := Classical.choice inferInstance
+  have heq := congrArg (fun X : Op I => X i i) M.sum_eq_one
+  simp [Matrix.sum_apply] at heq
+
+/-- Dilate both local POVM families of a strategy and pad its state by the two
+distinguished ancilla coordinates. -/
+private def projectiveDilation {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (a₀ : G.AnswerA) (b₀ : G.AnswerB) : Strategy G where
+  ιA := S.ιA × Option G.AnswerA
+  ιB := S.ιB × Option G.AnswerB

+  B := fun y => dilatedMeasurement b₀ (S.B y)
+
+/-- The local measurements of the Naimark-dilated strategy are projective. -/
+private theorem projectiveDilation_isProjective {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (a₀ : G.AnswerA) (b₀ : G.AnswerB) :
+    (projectiveDilation S a₀ b₀).IsProjective := by
+  constructor
+  · intro x

+/-- Form the block-diagonal direct sum of two POVMs with the same outcome type. -/
+private def blockMeasurement
+    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I)
+    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α J) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (Sum I J) :=
+  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
+    (fun a => MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock (A.effect a) (B.effect a))
+    (fun a => MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_nonneg (A.pos a) (B.pos a))
+    (by
+      calc
+        (∑ a : α, MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+            (A.effect a) (B.effect a)) =
+          MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+            (∑ a : α, A.effect a) (∑ a : α, B.effect a) := by
+              simpa using MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_finset_sum
+                Finset.univ A.effect B.effect
+        _ = 1 := by
+          rw [A.sum_eq_one, B.sum_eq_one,
+            MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_one])
+
+/-- A direct sum of projective POVMs is projective. -/
+private theorem blockMeasurement_isProjective
+    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I)
+    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α J)
+    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
+    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
+    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockMeasurement A B) := by
+  intro a
+  change IsProj (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+    (A.effect a) (B.effect a))
+  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
+  · change MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock (A.effect a) (B.effect a) *
+        MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock (A.effect a) (B.effect a) = _
+    rw [MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_mul,
+      (hA a).isIdempotentElem.eq, (hB a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
+  · change (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+        (A.effect a) (B.effect a))ᴴ = _
+    rw [MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_conjTranspose,
+      (hA a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
+      (hB a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]

+/-- Put a bipartite vector in the two exchanged off-diagonal sectors of the
+local direct sum, with equal amplitudes. -/
+private def symmState
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ (Sum I J × Sum I J) :=
+  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Sum I J × Sum I J) ℂ).symm fun p =>
+    match p with
+    | (Sum.inl i, Sum.inr j) => (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) * ψ.ofLp (i, j)
+    | (Sum.inr j, Sum.inl i) => (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) * ψ.ofLp (i, j)
+    | _ => 0
+
+/-- The direct-sum state is fixed by exchanging its two local tensor factors. -/
+private theorem symmState_swap
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
+    reindexState (Equiv.prodComm (Sum I J) (Sum I J)) (symmState ψ) =
+      symmState ψ := by
+  apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Sum I J × Sum I J) ℂ).injective
+  funext p
+  rcases p with ⟨p, q⟩
+  cases p <;> cases q <;> rfl
+
+/-- Coordinate formula for the direct-sum symmetric state. -/
+private theorem symmState_apply
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (p : Sum I J × Sum I J) :
+    (symmState ψ).ofLp p =
+      match p with
+      | (Sum.inl i, Sum.inr j) => (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) * ψ.ofLp (i, j)
+      | (Sum.inr j, Sum.inl i) => (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) * ψ.ofLp (i, j)
+      | _ => 0 := by
+  simp [symmState]
+
+/-- The equal-amplitude direct-sum symmetrization preserves the vector norm. -/
+private theorem symmState_norm
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) : ‖symmState ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖ := by
+  apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp
+  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
+  simp [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.sum_sum_type, symmState_apply]
+  rw [abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg 2)]
+  have hsqrt : (Real.sqrt 2 / 2) ^ 2 = (1 / 2 : ℝ) := by
+    rw [div_pow, Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]
+    norm_num
+  simp_rw [mul_pow, hsqrt]
+  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+  simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
+  ring_nf
+  exact Finset.sum_comm
+
+/-- Scaling both entries of a finite sesquilinear sum contributes the scalar
+`c * star c`. -/
+private theorem sesquilinear_sum_smul
+    {K L : Type*} [Fintype K] [Fintype L]
+    (c : ℂ) (f : K → L → ℂ) (v : L → ℂ) (w : K → ℂ) :
+    (∑ p : K, (∑ q : L, f p q * (c * v q)) * star (c * w p)) =
+      c * star c * ∑ p : K, (∑ q : L, f p q * v q) * star (w p) := by
+  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro p _
+  rw [star_mul]
+  have hinner : (∑ q : L, f p q * (c * v q)) =
+      c * ∑ q : L, f p q * v q := by
+    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro q _
+    ring
+  rw [hinner]
+  ring
+
+/-- A block tensor quadratic form on the symmetric state is the average of the
+two crossed quadratic forms on the original state. -/
+private theorem vectorQForm_symmState_block
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
+    (A C : Op I) (B D : Op J) :
+    vectorQForm (symmState ψ)
+        (heteroKron
+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock A B)
+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock C D)) =
+      (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+        (vectorQForm ψ (heteroKron A D) + vectorQForm ψ (heteroKron C B)) := by
+  unfold vectorQForm
+  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct,
+    EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
+  change Complex.re (∑ p : Sum I J × Sum I J,
+      (∑ q : Sum I J × Sum I J,
+        heteroKron
+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock A B)
+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock C D) p q *
+            (symmState ψ).ofLp q) * star (symmState ψ).ofLp p) =
+    (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+      (Complex.re (∑ p : I × J,
+          (∑ q : I × J, heteroKron A D p q * ψ.ofLp q) * star ψ.ofLp p) +
+        Complex.re (∑ p : I × J,
+          (∑ q : I × J, heteroKron C B p q * ψ.ofLp q) * star ψ.ofLp p))
+  simp only [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.sum_sum_type]
+  simp only [Pi.star_apply, symmState_apply]
+  simp only [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
+  simp only [
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inl_inl,
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inl_inr,
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inr_inl,
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inr_inr,
+    zero_mul, mul_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero, zero_add, add_zero]
+  let c : ℂ := Real.sqrt 2 / 2
+  have hfirst :
+      (∑ i : I, ∑ j : J,
+        (∑ k : I, ∑ l : J, A i k * D j l * (c * ψ.ofLp (k, l))) *
+          star (c * ψ.ofLp (i, j))) =
+        c * star c *
+          ∑ i : I, ∑ j : J,
+            (∑ k : I, ∑ l : J, A i k * D j l * ψ.ofLp (k, l)) *
+              star (ψ.ofLp (i, j)) := by
+    simpa only [Fintype.sum_prod_type, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
+      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply] using
+      (sesquilinear_sum_smul c (heteroKron A D) ψ.ofLp ψ.ofLp)
+  have hsecond :
+      (∑ j : J, ∑ i : I,
+        (∑ l : J, ∑ k : I, B j l * C i k * (c * ψ.ofLp (k, l))) *
+          star (c * ψ.ofLp (i, j))) =
+        c * star c *
+          ∑ j : J, ∑ i : I,
+            (∑ l : J, ∑ k : I, B j l * C i k * ψ.ofLp (k, l)) *
+              star (ψ.ofLp (i, j)) := by
+    simpa only [Fintype.sum_prod_type, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
+      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply] using
+      (sesquilinear_sum_smul c (heteroKron B C)
+        (fun p : J × I => ψ.ofLp (p.2, p.1))
+        (fun p : J × I => ψ.ofLp (p.2, p.1)))
+  have hswap :
+      (∑ j : J, ∑ i : I,
+        (∑ l : J, ∑ k : I, B j l * C i k * ψ.ofLp (k, l)) *
+          star (ψ.ofLp (i, j))) =
+        ∑ i : I, ∑ j : J,
+          (∑ k : I, ∑ l : J, C i k * B j l * ψ.ofLp (k, l)) *
+            star (ψ.ofLp (i, j)) := by
+    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro i _
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro j _
+    congr 1
+    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro k _
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro l _
+    ring
+  change Complex.re (_ + _) = _
+  rw [hfirst, hsecond, hswap]
+  have hstar : star c = c := by
+    simp [c]
+  rw [hstar]
+  have hsqrt : (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) * (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) = (1 / 2 : ℂ) := by
+    norm_cast
+    rw [← pow_two, div_pow, Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]
+    norm_num
+  change Complex.re ((c * c) * _ + (c * c) * _) = _
+  rw [show c * c = (1 / 2 : ℂ) by simpa [c] using hsqrt]
+  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
+  ring
+
+/-- A symmetric distribution gives the same average after exchanging the two
+coordinates, independently of redundant zero-weight support entries. -/
+private theorem avgOver_prod_swap_of_weight_symm
+    {X : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
+    (μ : Distribution (X × X))
+    (hμ : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x))
+    (f : X × X → ℝ) :
+    avgOver μ (fun xy => f (xy.2, xy.1)) = avgOver μ f := by
+  unfold avgOver
+  calc
+    (∑ xy ∈ μ.support, μ.weight xy * f (xy.2, xy.1)) =
+        ∑ xy : X × X, μ.weight xy * f (xy.2, xy.1) := by
+          symm
+          exact Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support μ _ fun xy hxy => by
+            rw [μ.outsideSupport xy hxy, zero_mul]
+    _ = ∑ x : X, ∑ y : X, μ.weight (x, y) * f (y, x) := by
+          rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    _ = ∑ y : X, ∑ x : X, μ.weight (x, y) * f (y, x) := Finset.sum_comm
+    _ = ∑ y : X, ∑ x : X, μ.weight (y, x) * f (y, x) := by
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro y _
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro x _
+          rw [hμ]
+    _ = ∑ xy : X × X, μ.weight xy * f xy := by
+          rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    _ = ∑ xy ∈ μ.support, μ.weight xy * f xy :=
+      Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support μ _ fun xy hxy => by
+        rw [μ.outsideSupport xy hxy, zero_mul]
+
+/-- Symmetrize a strategy by putting its two local spaces in a common direct
+sum and occupying the two exchanged tensor sectors with equal amplitude. -/
+private def symmetrizedStrategy {G : SymmetricGame}
+    (S : Strategy G.toGame) : SymmetricStrategy G where
+  ι := Sum S.ιA S.ιB
+  ψ := symmState S.ψ
+  ψ_norm := (symmState_norm S.ψ).trans S.ψ_norm
+  ψ_swap := symmState_swap S.ψ
+  M := fun x => blockMeasurement (S.A x) (S.B x)
+
+/-- Projectivity is preserved by direct-sum symmetrization. -/
+private theorem symmetrizedStrategy_isProjective {G : SymmetricGame}
+    (S : Strategy G.toGame) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
+    (symmetrizedStrategy S).toStrategy.IsProjective := by
+  constructor <;> intro x <;>
+    exact blockMeasurement_isProjective (S.A x) (S.B x) (hS.1 x) (hS.2 x)
+
+/-- The winning contribution of one question pair for a fixed strategy. -/
+private def strategyPayoff {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (xy : G.QuestionA × G.QuestionB) : ℝ :=
+  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
+    if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then
+      vectorQForm S.ψ (heteroKron ((S.A xy.1).effect a) ((S.B xy.2).effect b))
+    else 0
+
+/-- Strategy value is the question-distribution average of its pairwise payoff. -/
+private theorem strategy_value_eq_avgOver_payoff {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
+    S.value = avgOver G.μ (strategyPayoff S) := by
+  rfl
+
+/-- At a question pair, the symmetrized payoff is the average of the original
+payoff in the two question orders. -/
+private theorem symmetrizedStrategy_payoff {G : SymmetricGame}
+    (S : Strategy G.toGame) (x y : G.Question) :
+    strategyPayoff (symmetrizedStrategy S).toStrategy (x, y) =
+      (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+        (strategyPayoff S (x, y) + strategyPayoff S (y, x)) := by
+  unfold strategyPayoff
+  simp only [SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy, symmetrizedStrategy]
+  calc
+    (∑ a : G.Answer, ∑ b : G.Answer,
+      if G.decide x y a b then
+        vectorQForm (symmState S.ψ)
+          (heteroKron
+            ((blockMeasurement (S.A x) (S.B x)).effect a)
+            ((blockMeasurement (S.A y) (S.B y)).effect b))
+      else 0) =
+        ∑ a : G.Answer, ∑ b : G.Answer,
+          if G.decide x y a b then
+            (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+              (vectorQForm S.ψ
+                  (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) +
+                vectorQForm S.ψ
+                  (heteroKron ((S.A y).effect b) ((S.B x).effect a)))
+          else 0 := by
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro a _
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro b _
+            by_cases hab : G.decide x y a b
+            · simp only [hab, if_true]
+              simpa only [blockMeasurement,
+                MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne] using
+                vectorQForm_symmState_block S.ψ
+                  ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.A y).effect b)
+                  ((S.B x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
+            · simp [hab]
+    _ = (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+        ((∑ a : G.Answer, ∑ b : G.Answer,
+          if G.decide x y a b then
+            vectorQForm S.ψ
+              (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b))
+          else 0) +
+        (∑ a : G.Answer, ∑ b : G.Answer,
+          if G.decide x y a b then
+            vectorQForm S.ψ
+              (heteroKron ((S.A y).effect b) ((S.B x).effect a))
+          else 0)) := by
+            simp_rw [mul_add, Finset.mul_sum]
+            rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro a _
+            rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro b _
+            by_cases hab : G.decide x y a b <;> simp [hab]
+    _ = (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+        ((∑ a : G.Answer, ∑ b : G.Answer,
+          if G.decide x y a b then
+            vectorQForm S.ψ
+              (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b))
+          else 0) +
+        (∑ b : G.Answer, ∑ a : G.Answer,
+          if G.decide y x b a then
+            vectorQForm S.ψ
+              (heteroKron ((S.A y).effect b) ((S.B x).effect a))
+          else 0)) := by
+            congr 2
+            rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro b _
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro a _
+            rw [← G.decide_symm]
+
+/-- Symmetrization preserves the value of a strategy in a symmetric game. -/
+private theorem symmetrizedStrategy_value {G : SymmetricGame}
+    (S : Strategy G.toGame) :
+    (symmetrizedStrategy S).toStrategy.value = S.value := by
+  rw [strategy_value_eq_avgOver_payoff, strategy_value_eq_avgOver_payoff]
+  calc
+    avgOver G.μ (strategyPayoff (symmetrizedStrategy S).toStrategy) =
+        avgOver G.μ (fun xy => (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+          (strategyPayoff S xy + strategyPayoff S (xy.2, xy.1))) := by
+            apply avgOver_congr
+            intro xy
+            exact symmetrizedStrategy_payoff S xy.1 xy.2
+    _ = (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+        (avgOver G.μ (strategyPayoff S) +
+          avgOver G.μ (fun xy => strategyPayoff S (xy.2, xy.1))) := by
+            rw [avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_add]
+    _ = avgOver G.μ (strategyPayoff S) := by
+          change (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+            (avgOver G.μ (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S xy) +
+              avgOver G.μ
+                (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S (xy.2, xy.1))) =
+            avgOver G.μ (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S xy)
+          have hswapavg := avgOver_prod_swap_of_weight_symm G.μ G.μ_symm
+            (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S xy)
+          calc
+            (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+                (avgOver G.μ
+                    (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S xy) +
+                  avgOver G.μ (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question =>
+                    strategyPayoff S (xy.2, xy.1))) =
+              (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+                (avgOver G.μ
+                    (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S xy) +
+                  avgOver G.μ
+                    (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S xy)) :=
+                congrArg (fun z : ℝ => (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
+                  (avgOver G.μ (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question =>
+                    strategyPayoff S xy) + z)) hswapavg
+            _ = avgOver G.μ
+                (fun xy : G.Question × G.Question => strategyPayoff S xy) := by
+                  ring
+
+/-- A probability distribution has a nonempty ambient sample type. -/
+private theorem nonempty_of_probability {α : Type*}
+    (μ : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) : Nonempty α := by
+  classical
+  by_contra hα
+  haveI : IsEmpty α := not_nonempty_iff.mp hα
+  have hs : μ.support = ∅ := by
+    apply Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mpr
+    intro a
+    exact isEmptyElim a
+  have hsum := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one
+  rw [hs] at hsum
+  norm_num at hsum

   307	    either $\{A^x_a\}$ or $\{B^x_a\}$ is a projective measurement, then
   308	    $A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_{\delta^{1/2}} I_\alice \otimes B^x_a$.
   309	    \label{item:one-projector-implies-consistency}

   311	\end{fact}

   313	\begin{fact}[Fact 4.20 in~\cite{NW19}]
   314	  \label{fact:add-a-proj}
   315	  Let $\cal{A},\cal{B},\cal{C}$ be finite sets, and let $\mu$ be a distribution
   316	  over question pairs $(x,y)$.
   317	  Let $\{A_{a,b}^x\}$ and $\{B_{a,b}^x\}$ be operators whose outcomes range over the
   318	  product set $\cal{A} \times \cal{B}$.
   319	  Suppose a set of operators $\{C_{a,c}^y\}$, whose outcomes range over the
   320	  product set $\cal{A} \times \cal{C}$, satisfies the condition $\sum_{c}
   321	  (C_{a,c}^y)^\dagger C_{a,c}^y \leq \Id$ for all $a$ and all $y$.
   322	  If $A_{a,b}^x \approx_\delta B_{a,b}^x$ on average over $x$ sampled from the
   323	  corresponding marginal of distribution $\mu$, then $C^y_{a,c} A^x_{a,b}
   324	  \approx_\delta C^y_{a,c} B^x_{a,b}$ on average over $(x,y)$ sampled from $\mu$.
   325	\end{fact}
   326	\begin{proof}
   327	  Fix questions $x,y$ and answers $a \in \cal{A},b \in \cal{B}$. We have then that
   328	  \begin{align}
   329	    \sum_{c} \left \| (C^y_{a,c} A^x_{a,b} - C^y_{a,c} B^x_{a,b} ) \ket{\psi} \right \|^2
   330	    & = \sum_{c} \bra{\psi} (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})^\dagger (C^y_{a,c})^\dagger (C^y_{a,c})
   331	      (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b} ) \ket{\psi}\\
   332	    & \leq \bra{\psi} (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})^\dagger
   333	      (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b} ) \ket{\psi} \\
   334	    & = \left \| (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})\ket{\psi} \right \|^2
   335	  \end{align}
   336	  where the inequality follows from the assumption that $\sum_c (C_{a,c}^y)^\dagger
   337	  C_{a,c}^y \leq \Id$.
   338	  Thus we obtain the desired conclusion
   339	  \begin{equation*}
   340	    \E_{(x,y) \sim \mu} \sum_{a,b,c} \left \| (C^y_{a,c} A^x_{a,b} - C^y_{a,c} B^x_{a,b} )
   341	      \ket{\psi} \right \|^2 	\leq \E_{(x,y) \sim \mu} \sum_{a,b}
   342	    \left \| (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})\ket{\psi} \right \|^2 \leq \delta.
   343	  \end{equation*}
   344	\end{proof}

   347	\begin{fact}
   348	\label{fact:add-a-proj2}

Let $\{A^x_a \}$, $\{B^x_a\}$ be POVMs indexed by $\mathcal{X}$ and outcomes in $\mathcal{A}$.    355			\E_x \sum_g \norm{ S^x_g (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)}) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \sum_g \bra{\psi} (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)})^\dagger  (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)}) \ket{\psi} \\
   356			&= \E_x \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger  \Big(\sum_{g: g(x) = a} (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \Big) (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   357			&\leq \E_x \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   358			&= \E_x \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2.
   359		\end{align*}
   360		The inequality follows from the fact that $\sum_{g: g(x) = a} (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \leq \sum_g (S_g^x)^\dagger (S_g^x) \leq \Id$. The last line is at most $\delta$ by assumption, and we obtain the desired conclusion.

   364	\begin{lemma}
   365	\label{lem:cool-closeness-fact}
   366	Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{A}$ be finite sets and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. Let $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a projective measurement and let $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a set of matrices.    541	\subsection{The class $\MIP^*$}
   542	
   543	The complexity class $\MIP^*$ of \emph{multi-prover interactive proof
   544	  systems with entangled provers} is the class of languages that can be
   545	decided by a \emph{proof system} in which a polynomial-time classical
   546	\emph{verifier} interacts with noncommunicating, computationally unbounded
   547	 \emph{provers} who may share a \emph{finite-dimensional} entangled state. In general there may be polynomially many provers,
   548	and the verifier may interact with them over polynomially many
   549	rounds. In each round, the verifier generates a question for
   550	each prover and receives a response from them. At the end of
   551	the interaction the verifier 
   552	decides to either accept or reject. A language $L$ is in $\MIP^*$ if for
   553	every input $z \in L$, there exists a strategy that the provers can
   554	use to convince the verifier to accept with high probability ($\geq 2/3$), and for every input $z \not\in L$, there is
   555	\emph{no} strategy that the provers can use to convince the verifier
   556	to accept with more than low probability ($\geq 1/3$). The former
   557	property is called \emph{completeness} of the proof system, and the
   558	latter \emph{soundness}. The
   559	completeness and soundness probabilities $2/3$ and $1/3$ may be
   560	amplified by sequentially repeating the protocol.

docs/reports/issue-930-session48-orthonormalization-audit.md:78:The paper states the orthonormalization theorem for a permutation-invariant state and a submeasurement `A = {A_a}` satisfying strong self-consistency:
docs/reports/issue-930-session48-orthonormalization-audit.md:91:The Lean theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.orthonormalization` has the same mathematical conclusion, expressed as an `SDDRel` between the left lifts of `A` and `P.toSubMeas` with error `orthonormalizationError zeta = 100 * zeta^(1/4)` (`Defs.lean:288-290`, `Orthonormalization.lean:674-688`). The permutation-invariance hypothesis is explicit as `PermInvState psi`, and the pure-state normalization convention is explicit as `psi.IsNormalized`; this is the formal counterpart of the paper's vector state convention and is already documented in #933.
docs/reports/issue-930-session48-orthonormalization-audit.md:101:The proof route matches the paper reduction from submeasurements to measurements. Lean completes `A` to `optionCompletion A`, whose `none` outcome is `I - sum_a A_a` (`Statements.lean:164-190`). The lemma `optionCompletion_bipartiteSSCRel` proves the completed measurement is strongly self-consistent with error `2*zeta` (`Orthonormalization.lean:58-173`), exactly reflecting the paper's `1 - 2 zeta` lower bound at `orthonormalization.tex:339-354`. The returned projective submeasurement on `Option Outcome` is restricted back to the original outcomes by `restrictSomeProjSubMeas`, and `qSDD_liftLeft_restrictSomeProjSubMeas_le` records that dropping the extra nonnegative summand cannot increase the distance (`Orthonormalization.lean:35-56` and `175-227`). This is the formal version of the paper's definition `P_a = \widehat P_a` for `a` in the original outcome set.

 # Projective rounding for consistent POVMs
 
-This module derives an explicit finite-dimensional projective rounding from the
-Q/X/XHat construction used in the LDT orthonormalization theorem. The argument
-keeps the original Alice space and completes the resulting projective
-submeasurement after proving that its missing state mass is small.
+This module proves the orthonormalization lemma `lem:ortho` with an explicit
+error constant: if a POVM `Q` on Alice's space and a POVM `R` on Bob's space are
+`δ`-consistent on a unit bipartite state `ψ`, then Alice has a projective
+measurement `P` on her original space with `P_a ⊗ 1` within `220 · δ^(1/4)` of
+`Q_a ⊗ 1` on `ψ`.
+
+The argument passes to Alice's reduced state and follows the construction of the
+LDT orthonormalization theorem. Rounding the almost-projective effects of `Q` and
+reducing their ranks gives a family of projectors `Q_a` whose ranges are almost
+orthogonal; assembling those ranges into one auxiliary space gives an operator
+`X`, whose positive-Gram polar factor `X̂` is a coisometry; and pulling the block
+projector of each outcome back along `X̂`, so that `P_a = X̂ᴴ T_a X̂`, gives a
+projective family close to `Q`. The family `P` lives on Alice's original space
+and is completed to a measurement at one fixed outcome once its missing state
+mass has been shown to be small.

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Consistency
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.State

/-! # Strategy classes and symmetric games

This module defines projective, commuting, consistent, PCC, and SPCC strategy
predicates from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:89-183`, with source
definitions in `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-180`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

universe u

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- Projectivity from `def:projective-strategy-general`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:90-101`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`. -/
def Strategy.IsProjective {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.A x)) ∧
    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.B y)

/-- Symmetric games from `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`.
The question and answer alphabets are each represented by a single shared type,
matching the source notation. -/
structure SymmetricGame where
  Question : Type
  Answer : Type
  [questionFintype : Fintype Question]
  [answerFintype : Fintype Answer]
  [questionDecidableEq : DecidableEq Question]
  [answerDecidableEq : DecidableEq Answer]
  μ : Distribution (Question × Question)
  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
  μ_symm : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x)
  decide : Question → Question → Answer → Answer → Bool
  decide_symm : ∀ x y a b, decide x y a b = decide y x b a

attribute [instance] SymmetricGame.questionFintype SymmetricGame.answerFintype
  SymmetricGame.questionDecidableEq SymmetricGame.answerDecidableEq

/-- Regard a symmetric game as a game with equal question and answer types;
`def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
def SymmetricGame.toGame (G : SymmetricGame) : Game where
  QuestionA := G.Question
  QuestionB := G.Question
  AnswerA := G.Answer
  AnswerB := G.Answer
  μ := G.μ
  μ_prob := G.μ_prob
  decide := G.decide

/-- Symmetric strategies from `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`.
The two local spaces and measurement families are identified, as in the source
definition. -/
structure SymmetricStrategy (G : SymmetricGame) where
  ι : Type
  [ιFintype : Fintype ι]
  [ιDecidableEq : DecidableEq ι]
  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)
  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
  ψ_swap : reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) ψ = ψ
  M : G.Question → Measurement G.Answer ι

attribute [instance] SymmetricStrategy.ιFintype SymmetricStrategy.ιDecidableEq

/-- Regard a symmetric strategy as a strategy using the same local space and
measurement family for both players; `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
def SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy {G : SymmetricGame} (S : SymmetricStrategy G) :
    Strategy G.toGame where
  ιA := S.ι
  ιB := S.ι
  ψ := S.ψ
  ψ_norm := S.ψ_norm
  A := S.M
  B := S.M

/-- Common-space commutation from `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:141-150`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
def IsCommutingOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β]
    [DecidableEq β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution (X × Y)) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
    (B : Y → Measurement β ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y, 0 < μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((B y).effect b)

private def transportOp {d₁ d₂ : Type u} (h : d₁ = d₂) (M : Op d₂) : Op d₁ :=
  h.symm ▸ M

/-- Transported common-space form of `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:141-150`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
def Strategy.IsCommuting {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (hι : S.ιA = S.ιB) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y, 0 < G.μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b,
    Commute ((S.A x).effect a) (transportOp hι ((S.B y).effect b))

/-- Measurement consistency from `def:consistent-measurement`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:152-161`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:144-160`. -/
def Measurement.IsConsistentOn {α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, (heteroKron (M.effect a) 1).mulVec ψ =
    (heteroKron 1 (M.effect a)).mulVec ψ

/-- General strategy consistency from `def:consistent-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:169-174`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
def IsConsistentStrategyOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B : Y → Measurement β ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (A x) ψ) ∧
    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (B y) ψ

/-- Symmetric strategy consistency from `def:consistent-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:169-174`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
def SymmetricStrategy.IsConsistent {G : SymmetricGame}
    (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (S.M x) S.ψ

/-- The PCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:178-183`,
paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:176-180`. -/
def Strategy.IsPCC {G : Game} {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution (G.QuestionA × G.QuestionB))
    (A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ι)
    (B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ι)
  (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A x)) ∧
    (∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (B y)) ∧
    IsConsistentStrategyOn A B ψ ∧ IsCommutingOn μ A B

/-- The SPCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:178-183`,
paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:176-180`. -/
def SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC {G : SymmetricGame}
  (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.M x)) ∧ S.IsConsistent ∧
    IsCommutingOn G.μ S.M S.M

/-- Source symmetrization statement `lem:symmetric-strat`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:116-135`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-130`.
The attainment defect is `rem:symmetric-strat-limit` and is tracked in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_symmetrization-attainment.tex`. -/
theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy (G : SymmetricGame) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (h : G.toGame.value = 1 - ε) :
    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
      1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
  sorry

/-- Value-preserving formalization-only form of `lem:symmetric-strat` starting
from a specified near-optimal strategy; blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:116-135`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-130`.
The source attainment distinction is tracked in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_symmetrization-attainment.tex`. -/
theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy_of_strategy (G : SymmetricGame)
    (ε : ℝ) (S₀ : Strategy G.toGame) (h : 1 - ε ≤ S₀.value) :
    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
      S.toStrategy.value = S₀.value ∧ 1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
  sorry

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   249	/-- Simultaneously reindexing a state and an operator preserves their quadratic form. -/
   250	private theorem stateQForm_reindex
   251	    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   252	    (e : I ≃ J) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) (M : Op I) :
   253	    stateQForm (reindexState e ψ) (reindexOp e.symm M) = stateQForm ψ M := by
   254	  have hstate (j : J) : (reindexState e ψ).ofLp j = ψ.ofLp (e.symm j) := by
   255	    rfl
   256	  have hstate_star (j : J) : star (reindexState e ψ).ofLp j =
   257	      star (ψ.ofLp (e.symm j)) := congrArg star (hstate j)
   258	  have hop (j k : J) : reindexOp e.symm M j k = M (e.symm j) (e.symm k) := by
   259	    rfl
   260	  unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState
   261	  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   262	  change (Complex.re (∑ j : J,
   263	      (∑ k : J, reindexOp e.symm M j k * (reindexState e ψ).ofLp k) *
   264	        star (reindexState e ψ).ofLp j)) =
   265	    Complex.re (∑ i : I, (∑ k : I, M i k * ψ.ofLp k) * star (ψ.ofLp i))
   266	  simp_rw [hop, hstate, hstate_star]
   267	  apply congrArg Complex.re
   268	  have hinner (j : J) :
   269	      (∑ k : J, M (e.symm j) (e.symm k) * ψ.ofLp (e.symm k)) =
   270	        ∑ k : I, M (e.symm j) k * ψ.ofLp k :=
   271	    e.symm.sum_comp (fun k : I => M (e.symm j) k * ψ.ofLp k)
   272	  calc
   273	    (∑ j : J, (∑ k : J, M (e.symm j) (e.symm k) * ψ.ofLp (e.symm k)) *
   274	        star (ψ.ofLp (e.symm j))) =
   275	      ∑ j : J, (∑ k : I, M (e.symm j) k * ψ.ofLp k) *
   276	        star (ψ.ofLp (e.symm j)) := by simp_rw [hinner]
   277	    _ = ∑ i : I, (∑ k : I, M i k * ψ.ofLp k) * star (ψ.ofLp i) :=
   278	      e.symm.sum_comp (fun i : I => (∑ k : I, M i k * ψ.ofLp k) * star (ψ.ofLp i))

   280	/-- The product POVM whose effects are Kronecker products of the two factor effects. -/
   281	private noncomputable def tensorMeasurement
   282	    {α β I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   283	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   284	    (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement β J) :
   285	    Measurement (α × β) (I × J) :=
   286	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   287	    (fun ab => heteroKron (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2))
   288	    (fun ab => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (A.pos ab.1) (B.pos ab.2))
   289	    (by
   290	      change ∑ ab : α × β, opTensor (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) = 1
   291	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   292	      calc
   293	        (∑ a : α, ∑ b : β, opTensor (A.effect a) (B.effect b)) =
   294	            ∑ a : α, leftTensor (A.effect a) *
   295	              (∑ b : β, rightTensor (B.effect b)) := by
   296	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   297	          intro a _
   298	          rw [Matrix.mul_sum]
   299	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   300	          intro b _
   301	          exact (leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor _ _).symm
   302	        _ = 1 := by
   303	          rw [rightTensor_finset_sum, B.sum_eq_one, rightTensor_one]
   304	          simp_rw [Matrix.mul_one]
   305	          rw [leftTensor_finset_sum, A.sum_eq_one, leftTensor_one])

   307	/-- The product of two projective POVMs is projective. -/
   308	private theorem tensorMeasurement_isProjective
   309	    {α β I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   310	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   311	    (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement β J)
   312	    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
   313	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
   314	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (tensorMeasurement A B) := by
   315	  intro ab
   316	  change IsProj (Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2))
   317	  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
   318	  · calc
   319	      Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) *
   320	          Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) =
   321	        Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1 * A.effect ab.1)
   322	          (B.effect ab.2 * B.effect ab.2) := by
   323	            simpa using (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul (A.effect ab.1) (A.effect ab.1)
   324	              (B.effect ab.2) (B.effect ab.2)).symm
   325	      _ = Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) := by
   326	        rw [(hA ab.1).isIdempotentElem.eq, (hB ab.2).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   327	  · exact (Matrix.IsHermitian.ext fun i j => by
   328	      rcases i with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
   329	      rcases j with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
   330	      simp [Matrix.kronecker, (hA ab.1).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.apply,
   331	        (hB ab.2).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.apply]).isSelfAdjoint

   333	/-- Transport a POVM along an equivalence of its finite-dimensional coordinate type. -/
   334	private noncomputable def reindexMeasurement
   335	    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α]
   336	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   337	    (e : I ≃ J) (M : Measurement α J) : Measurement α I :=
   338	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   339	    (fun a => reindexOp e (M.effect a))
   340	    (fun a => MIPStarRE.Quantum.reindex_nonneg e.symm (M.pos a))
   341	    (by
   342	      change ∑ a : α, (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ e.symm) (M.effect a) = 1
   343	      rw [← map_sum, M.sum_eq_one, map_one])

   347	    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α]

   349	    (e : I ≃ J) (M : Measurement α J)

   363	/-- The sum of the squared effects of a POVM is bounded by the identity. -/

   365	    {α I : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]

   414	/-- Tensoring a left-side POVM perturbation with a fixed right POVM does not

   417	    {X Y α β I J : Type*} [DecidableEq X]

   419	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   420	    (μ : Distribution (X × Y)) (A A' : X → Measurement α I)
   421	    (B : Y → Measurement β J) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (δ : ℝ)
   422	    (h : opFamilyDistSq (μ.map Prod.fst)
   423	      (fun x a => leftTensor ((A x).effect a))
   424	      (fun x a => leftTensor ((A' x).effect a)) ψ ≤ δ) :
   425	    opFamilyDistSq μ
   426	      (fun xy ab => (tensorMeasurement (A xy.1) (B xy.2)).effect ab)
   427	      (fun xy ab => (tensorMeasurement (A' xy.1) (B xy.2)).effect ab) ψ ≤ δ := by
   428	  unfold opFamilyDistSq at h ⊢
   429	  calc
   430	    avgOver μ (fun xy => ∑ ab : α × β,
   431	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   432	          ((tensorMeasurement (A xy.1) (B xy.2)).effect ab -
   433	            (tensorMeasurement (A' xy.1) (B xy.2)).effect ab) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤
   434	      avgOver μ (fun xy => ∑ a : α,
   435	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   436	          (leftTensor ((A xy.1).effect a) - leftTensor ((A' xy.1).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2) := by
   437	      apply avgOver_mono
   438	      intro xy
   439	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   440	      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   441	      intro a _
   442	      have hcontract := sum_norm_mul_apply_le
   443	        (fun b : β => rightTensor (ι₁ := I) ((B xy.2).effect b))
   444	        (leftTensor ((A xy.1).effect a) - leftTensor ((A' xy.1).effect a)) ψ
   445	        (rightPlacedMeasurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one (I := I) (B xy.2))
   446	      apply le_trans ?_ hcontract
   447	      apply le_of_eq
   448	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   449	      intro b _
   450	      change ‖applyOperatorToState
   451	          (opTensor ((A xy.1).effect a) ((B xy.2).effect b) -
   452	            opTensor ((A' xy.1).effect a) ((B xy.2).effect b)) ψ‖ ^ 2 = _
   453	      congr 2
   454	      rw [Matrix.mul_sub, rightTensor_mul_leftTensor_eq_opTensor,
   455	        rightTensor_mul_leftTensor_eq_opTensor, opTensor_sub_left]
   456	    _ = avgOver (μ.map Prod.fst) (fun x => ∑ a : α,
   457	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   458	          (leftTensor ((A x).effect a) - leftTensor ((A' x).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2) := by
   459	      exact (Distribution.avgOver_map μ Prod.fst (fun x => ∑ a : α,
   460	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   461	          (leftTensor ((A x).effect a) - leftTensor ((A' x).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2)).symm
   462	    _ ≤ δ := h

   545	      |S.value - S'.value| ≤ C₀ * Real.rpow δ (1 / 2 : ℝ) := by
   546	  refine ⟨4, by norm_num, ?_⟩
   547	  intro G S S' δ hδ0 _hδ1 hclose hstate hprojective
   548	  let eA : S.ιA ≃ S'.ιA := Equiv.cast hclose.hA
   549	  let eB : S.ιB ≃ S'.ιB := Equiv.cast hclose.hB
   550	  let A' : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA S.ιA :=
   551	    fun x => reindexMeasurement eA (S'.A x)
   552	  let B' : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB S.ιB :=
   553	    fun y => reindexMeasurement eB (S'.B y)

   555	    convert hstate using 1
   556	    ext ij
   557	    rfl
   558	  let JS : G.QuestionA × G.QuestionB → G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB →
   559	      Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) := fun xy ab =>
   560	    (tensorMeasurement (S.A xy.1) (S.B xy.2)).effect ab
   561	  let JM : G.QuestionA × G.QuestionB → G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB →
   562	      Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) := fun xy ab =>
   563	    (tensorMeasurement (S.A xy.1) (B' xy.2)).effect ab
